files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.BaseProtocol.ActionMessage
files.Summary: A general message serves as an envelope carrying an action to be transmitted between the client and the server via a DiagramServer.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.BaseProtocol.BaseAction
files.Summary: An action is a declarative description of a behavior that shall be invoked by the receiver upon receipt of the action. It is a plain data structure, and as such transferable between server and client. Actions contained in action messages are identified by their kind attribute. This attribute is required for all actions. Certain actions are meant to be sent from the client to the server or vice versa, while other actions can be sent both ways, by the client or the server. All actions must extend the default action interface.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.BaseProtocol.CompoundOperation
files.Summary: An operation that executes a list of operations.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.BaseProtocol.CustomOperation

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.BaseProtocol.ExecutableAction
files.Summary: Denotes an action that can be executed

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.BaseProtocol.Operation
files.Summary: Marker interface for operations.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.BaseProtocol.RejectAction
files.Summary: A reject action is a response fired to indicate that a request must be rejected.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.BaseProtocol.RequestAction
files.Summary: A request action is tied to the expectation of receiving a corresponding response action. The requestId property is used to match the received response with the original request.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.BaseProtocol.ResponseAction
files.Summary: A response action is sent to respond to a request action. The responseId must match the requestId of the preceding request. In case the responseId is empty or undefined, the action is handled as standalone, i.e. it was fired without a preceding request.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Clipboard.CutOperation
files.Summary: Requests a cut operation from the server, i.e., deleting the selected elements from the model. Before submitting a CutOperation a client should ensure that the cut elements are put into the clipboard.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Clipboard.PasteOperation
files.Summary: Requests a paste operation from the server by providing the current clipboard data. Typically this means that elements should be created based on the data in the clipboard.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Clipboard.RequestClipboardDataAction
files.Summary: Requests the clipboard data for the current editor context, i.e., the selected elements, in a clipboard-compatible format.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Clipboard.SetClipboardDataAction
files.Summary: Server response to a RequestClipboardDataAction containing the selected elements as clipboard-compatible format.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Context.Contexts
files.Summary: Helper class to contain default context ids

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Context.RequestContextActions
files.Summary: The RequestContextActions is sent from the client to the server to request the available actions for the context with id contextId.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Context.SetContextActions
files.Summary: The SetContextActions is the response to a RequestContextActions containing all actions for the queried context.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Context.TriggerEdgeCreationAction
files.Summary: Triggers the enablement of the tool that is responsible for creating edges and initializes it with the creation of edges of the given elementTypeId.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Context.TriggerNodeCreationAction
files.Summary: Triggers the enablement of the tool that is responsible for creating nodes and initializes it with the creation of nodes of the given elementTypeId.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Layout.CenterAction
files.Summary: Centers the viewport on the elements with the given identifiers. It changes the scroll setting of the viewport accordingly and resets the zoom to its default. This action can also be created on the client but it can also be sent by the server in order to perform such a viewport change remotely.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Layout.ComputedBoundsAction
files.Summary: Sent from the client to the server to transmit the result of bounds computation as a response to a RequestBoundsAction. If the server is responsible for parts of the layout, it can do so after applying the computed bounds received with this action. Otherwise there is no need to send the computed bounds to the server, so they can be processed locally by the client.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Layout.FitToScreenAction
files.Summary: Triggers to fit all or a list of elements into the available drawing area. The resulting fit-to-screen command changes the zoom and scroll settings of the viewport so the model can be shown completely. This action can also be sent from the server to the client in order to perform such a viewport change programmatically.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Layout.LayoutOperation
files.Summary: Request a layout of the diagram or selected elements from the server.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Layout.LayoutOptions
files.Summary: Denotes layout options for nodes

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Layout.RequestBoundsAction
files.Summary: Sent from the server to the client to request bounds for the given model. The model is rendered invisibly so the bounds can derived from the DOM. The response is a ComputedBoundsAction. This hidden rendering round-trip is necessary if the client is responsible for parts of the layout.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Layout.RoundedCornerOptions
files.Summary: Denotes layout options for the rounded corner view

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Lifecycle.ClientState
files.Summary: Denotes the state of the client

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Lifecycle.InitializeResult
files.Summary: The initial server response after a client connected

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.ModelData.ExportSvgAction
files.Summary: The client sends an ExportSvgAction to indicate that the diagram, which represents the current model state, should be exported in SVG format. The action only provides the diagram SVG as plain string. The expected result of executing an ExportSvgAction is a new file in SVG-format on the underlying filesystem. However, other details like the target destination, concrete file name, file extension etc. are not specified in the protocol. So it is the responsibility of the action handler to process this information accordingly and export the result to the underlying filesystem.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.ModelData.ModelEditModes
files.Summary: Container for edit modes

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.ModelData.RequestExportSvgAction
files.Summary: A RequestExportSvgAction is sent by the client (or the server) to initiate the SVG export of the current diagram. The handler of this action is expected to retrieve the diagram SVG and should send an ExportSvgAction as response. Typically the ExportSvgAction is handled directly on client side.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.ModelData.RequestModelAction
files.Summary: Sent from the client to the server in order to request a graphical model. Usually this is the first message that is sent from the client to the server, so it is also used to initiate the communication. The response is a SetModelAction or an UpdateModelAction.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.ModelData.SaveModelAction
files.Summary: Sent from the client to the server in order to persist the current model state back to the source model. A new fileUri can be defined to save the model to a new destination different from its original source model.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.ModelData.SetDirtyAction
files.Summary: The server sends a SetDirtyStateAction to indicate to the client that the current model state on the server does not correspond to the persisted model state of the source model. A client may ignore such an action or use it to indicate to the user the dirty state.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.ModelData.SetEditModeAction
files.Summary: Sent from the client to the server to set the model into a specific editor mode, allowing the server to react to certain requests differently depending on the mode. A client may also listen to this action to prevent certain user interactions preemptively.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.ModelData.SetModelAction
files.Summary: ent from the server to the client in order to set the model. If a model is already present, it is replaced.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.ModelData.SourceModelChangedAction
files.Summary: Sent from the server to the client in order to indicate that the source model has changed. The source model denotes the data source from which the diagram has been originally derived (such as a file, a database, etc.). Typically clients would react to such an action by asking the user whether she wants to reload the diagram or ignore the changes and continue editing. If the editor has no changes (i.e. is not dirty), clients may also choose to directly refresh the editor by sending a RequestModelAction.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.ModelData.UpdateModelAction
files.Summary: Sent from the server to the client in order to update the model. If no model is present yet, this behaves the same as a SetModelAction. The transition from the old model to the new one can be animated.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Modification.ApplyLabelEditOperation
files.Summary: A very common use case in domain models is the support of labels that display textual information to the user. For instance, the GGraph model has support for labels that can be attached to a node, edge, or port, and that contain some text that is rendered in the view. To apply new text to such a label element the client may send an ApplyLabelEditOperation to the server.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Modification.ChangeBoundsOperation
files.Summary: Triggers the position or size change of elements. This action concerns only the element’s graphical size and position. Whether an element can be resized or repositioned may be specified by the server with a TypeHint to allow for immediate user feedback before resizing or repositioning.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Modification.ChangeContainerOperation
files.Summary: The client sends a ChangeContainerOperation to the server to request the execution of a changeContainer operation.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Modification.ChangeRoutingPointsOperation
files.Summary: An edge may have zero or more routing points that “re-direct” the edge between the source and the target element. In order to set these routing points the client may send a ChangeRoutingPointsOperation.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Modification.CreateEdgeOperation
files.Summary: In order to create an edge in the model the client can send a CreateEdgeOperation with the necessary information to create that edge.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Modification.CreateNodeOperation
files.Summary: In order to create a node in the model the client can send a CreateNodeOperation with the necessary information to create that node.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Modification.DeleteElementOperation
files.Summary: The client sends a DeleteElementOperation to the server to request the deletion of an element from the model.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Modification.ReconnectEdgeOperation
files.Summary: If the source and/or target element of an edge should be adapted, the client can send a ReconnectEdgeOperation to the server.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Navigation.NavigateToExternalTargetAction
files.Summary: If a navigation target cannot be resolved or the resolved target is something that is not part of our source model, e.g., a separate documentation file, a NavigateToExternalTargetAction may be sent. Since the target it outside of the model scope such an action would be typically handled by an integration layer (such as the surrounding IDE).

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Navigation.NavigateToTargetAction
files.Summary: Action that triggers the navigation to a particular navigation target. This may be used by the client internally or may be sent from the server.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Navigation.NavigationTarget
files.Summary: A NavigationTarget identifies the object we want to navigate to via its uri and may further provide a label to display for the client. Additionally, generic arguments may be used to to encode any domain- or navigation type-specific information.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Navigation.RequestNavigationTargetsAction
files.Summary: Action that is usually sent from the client to the server to request navigation targets for a specific navigation type such as documentation or implementation in the given editor context.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Navigation.ResolveNavigationTargetAction
files.Summary: If a client cannot navigate to a target directly, a ResolveNavigationTargetAction may be sent to the server to resolve the navigation target to one or more model elements. This may be useful in cases where the resolution of each target is expensive or the client architecture requires an indirection.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Navigation.SetNavigationTargetsAction
files.Summary: Response action from the server following a RequestNavigationTargetsAction. It contains all available navigation targets for the queried target type in the provided editor context. The server may also provide additional information using the arguments, e.g., warnings, that can be interpreted by the client.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Navigation.SetResolvedNavigationTargetAction
files.Summary: An action sent from the server in response to a ResolveNavigationTargetAction. The response contains the resolved element ids for the given target and may contain additional information in the args property.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Notification.EndProgressAction
files.Summary: This action is sent by the server to the client to end the reporting of a progress.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Notification.MessageAction
files.Summary: This action is typically sent by the server (or the client) to notify the user about something of interest.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Notification.SeverityLevels
files.Summary: The severity of a status or message.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Notification.StartProgressAction
files.Summary: This action is sent by the server to the client to request presenting the progress of a long running process in the UI.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Notification.StatusAction
files.Summary: This action is typically sent by the server (or the client) to signal a state change. If a timeout is given the respective status should disappear after the timeout is reached.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Notification.UpdateProgressAction
files.Summary: This action is sent by the server to the client to presenting an update of the progress of a long running process in the UI.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Selection.RequestPopupModelAction
files.Summary: Triggered when the user hovers the mouse pointer over an element to get a popup with details on that element. This action is sent from the client to the server. The response is a SetPopupModelAction.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Selection.SelectAction
files.Summary: Triggered when the user changes the selection, e.g. by clicking on a selectable element. The action should trigger a change in the selected state accordingly, so the elements can be rendered differently. The server can send such an action to the client in order to change the selection remotely.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Selection.SelectAllAction
files.Summary: Used for selecting or deselecting all elements.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Selection.SetPopupModelAction
files.Summary: Sent from the server to the client to display a popup in response to a RequestPopupModelAction. This action can also be used to remove any existing popup by choosing EMPTY_ROOT as root element.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Types.Bounds
files.Summary: The bounds are the position (x, y) and dimension (width, height) of an object. As such the Bounds type extends both Point and Dimension.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Types.CheckEdgeResultAction
files.Summary: Sent from the server to the client as a response for a { RequestCheckEdgeAction}. It provides a boolean indicating whether the edge context information provided by the corresponding request action is valid i.e. creation of an edge with the given edge type and source/target element is allowed.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Types.Dimension
files.Summary: The Dimension of an object is composed of its width and height.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Types.EdgeLabelPlacement
files.Summary: Denotes the placement of a label relative to an edge

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Types.EdgeTypeHint
files.Summary: Type hints for edges

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Types.EditorContext
files.Summary: The EditorContext may be used to represent the current state of the editor for particular actions. It encompasses the last recorded mouse position, the list of selected elements, and may contain custom arguments to encode additional state information.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Types.ElementAndAlignment
files.Summary: The ElementAndAlignment type is used to associate a new alignment with a model element, which is referenced via its id.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Types.ElementAndBounds
files.Summary: The ElementAndBounds type is used to associate new bounds with a model element, which is referenced via its id.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Types.ElementAndRoutingPoints
files.Summary: The ElementAndRoutingPoints type is used to associate an edge with specific routing points.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Types.LabeledAction
files.Summary: Labeled actions are used to denote a group of actions in a user-interface context, e.g., to define an entry in the command palette or in the context menu.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Types.Point
files.Summary: A Point is composed of the (x,y) coordinates of an object.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Types.RequestCheckEdgeAction
files.Summary: Sent from the client to the server to check wether the provided edge context information is valid i.e. creation of an edge with the given edge type and source/target element is allowed by the server. Typically this action is dispatched by edge creation tools in the creation phase of an edge that’s associated with a dynamic EdgeTypeHint.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Types.RequestTypeHintsAction
files.Summary: Sent from the client to the server in order to request hints on whether certain modifications are allowed for a specific element type. The RequestTypeHintsAction is optional, but should usually be among the first messages sent from the client to the server after receiving the model via RequestModelAction. The response is a SetTypeHintsAction.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Types.SetTypeHintsAction
files.Summary: Sent from the server to the client in order to provide hints certain modifications are allowed for a specific element type.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Types.ShapeTypeHint
files.Summary: Type hints for shapes

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Types.TypeHint
files.Summary: Type hints are used to define what modifications are supported on the different element types. Conceptually type hints are similar to features of a model elements but define the functionality on a type level. The rationale is to avoid a client-server round-trip for user feedback of each synchronous user interaction.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.UndoRedo.RedoAction
files.Summary: Trigger a redo of the latest undone command.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.UndoRedo.UndoAction
files.Summary: Trigger an undo of the latest executed command.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Validation.DeleteMarkersAction
files.Summary: To remove markers for elements a client or server may send a DeleteMarkersAction with all markers that should be removed.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Validation.Marker
files.Summary: A marker represents the validation result for a single model element.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Validation.MarkerKind
files.Summary: The severity of a Marker.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Validation.RequestEditValidationAction
files.Summary: Requests the validation of the given text in the context of the provided model element. Typically sent from the client to the server.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Validation.RequestMarkersAction
files.Summary: Action to retrieve markers for the specified model elements. Sent from the client to the server.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Validation.ResponseError
files.Summary: A validation error

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Validation.SetEditValidationResultAction
files.Summary: Response to a RequestEditValidationAction containing the validation result for applying a text on a certain model element.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Validation.SetMarkersAction
files.Summary: Response to the RequestMarkersAction containing all validation markers. Sent from the server to the client. This action always sends the entire list of markers. Thus, clients can replace all markers for a specific reason with the new ones that have been sent with the same reason.

files.Title: NMF.Glsp.Protocol.Validation.ValidationStatus
files.Summary: Denotes the validation status for editing text

An association describes a set of tuples whose values refer to typed instances. An instance of an association is called a link. files.Summary:

Certain kinds of constraints (such as an association "xor" constraint) are predefined in UML, others may be user-defined. A user-defined Constraint is described using a specified language, whose syntax and interpretation is a tool responsibility. One predefined language for writing constraints is OCL. In some situations, a programming language such as Java may be appropriate for expressing a constraint. In other situations natural language may be used.

Constraint is a condition (a Boolean expression) that restricts the extension of the associated element beyond what is imposed by the other language constructs applied to the element. Constraint contains an optional name, although they are commonly unnamed.

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Legacy.Cmof.PackageMerge
files.Summary:
A package merge is a directed relationship between two packages, that indicates that the contents of the two packages are to be combined. It is very similar to Generalization in the sense that the source element conceptually adds the characteristics of the target element to its own characteristics resulting in an element that combines the characteristics of both.

This mechanism should be used when elements defined in different packages have the same name and are intended to represent the same concept. Most often it is used to provide different definitions of a given concept for different purposes, starting from a common base definition. A given base concept is extended in increments, with each increment defined in a separate merged package. By selecting which increments to merge, it is possible to obtain a custom definition of a concept for a specific end. Package merge is particularly useful in meta-modeling and is extensively used in the definition of the UML metamodel.

Conceptually, a package merge can be viewed as an operation that takes the contents of two packages and produces a new package that combines the contents of the packages involved in the merge. In terms of model semantics, there is no difference between a model with explicit package merges, and a model in which all the merges have been performed.

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Legacy.Cmof.ParameterDirectionKind
files.Summary:
ParameterDirectionKind is an enumeration of the following literal values:

  • in Indicates that parameter values are passed into the behavioral element by the caller.

  • inout Indicates that parameter values are passed into a behavioral element by the caller and then back out to the caller from the behavioral element.

  • out Indicates that parameter values are passed from a behavioral element out to the caller.

  • return Indicates that parameter values are passed as return values from a behavioral element back to the caller.

In Core and the UML metamodel, these primitive types are predefined and available to the Core and UML extensions at all time. These predefined value types are independent of any object model and part of the definition of the Core.

A primitive type is a data type implemented by the underlying infrastructure and made available for modeling.

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.Deployment
files.Summary: A deployment is the allocation of an artifact or artifact instance to a deployment target. A component deployment is the deployment of one or more artifacts or artifact instances to a deployment target, optionally parameterized by a deployment specification. Examples are executables and configuration files. <p>From package UML::Deployments.</p>

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.DeploymentClientCollection
files.Summary: The collection class to implement the refined client reference for the Deployment class

files.Summary: Denotes a class to implement the configuration reference

files.Summary: The collection class to to represent the children of the DeploymentSpecification class

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.DeploymentSpecification
files.Summary: A deployment specification specifies a set of properties that determine execution parameters of a component artifact that is deployed on a node. A deployment specification can be aimed at a specific type of container. An artifact that reifies or implements deployment specification properties is a deployment descriptor. <p>From package UML::Deployments.</p>

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.DeploymentSupplierCollection
files.Summary: The collection class to implement the refined supplier reference for the Deployment class

files.Summary: The collection class to to represent the children of the DeploymentTarget class

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.DeploymentTarget
files.Summary: A deployment target is the location for a deployed artifact. <p>From package UML::Deployments.</p>

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.DeploymentTargetDeploymentCollection
files.Summary: Denotes a class to implement the deployment reference

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.DestroyLinkAction
files.Summary: A DestroyLinkAction is a WriteLinkAction that destroys links (including link objects). <p>From package UML::Actions.</p>

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.DestroyObjectAction.DestroyObjectActionChildrenCollection
files.Summary: The collection class to to represent the children of the DestroyObjectAction class

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.DestroyObjectAction.DestroyObjectActionReferencedElementsCollection
files.Summary: The collection class to to represent the children of the DestroyObjectAction class

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.DestroyObjectAction
files.Summary: A DestroyObjectAction is an Action that destroys objects. <p>From package UML::Actions.</p>

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.DestructionOccurrenceSpecification
files.Summary: A DestructionOccurenceSpecification models the destruction of an object. <p>From package UML::Interactions.</p>

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.Device
files.Summary: A device is a physical computational resource with processing capability upon which artifacts may be deployed for execution. Devices may be complex (i.e., they may consist of other devices). <p>From package UML::Deployments.</p>

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.DirectedRelationship
files.Summary: A DirectedRelationship represents a relationship between a collection of source model Elements and a collection of target model Elements. <p>From package UML::CommonStructure.</p>

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.Duration.DurationChildrenCollection
files.Summary: The collection class to to represent the children of the Duration class

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.Duration.DurationReferencedElementsCollection
files.Summary: The collection class to to represent the children of the Duration class

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.Duration
files.Summary: A Duration is a ValueSpecification that specifies the temporal distance between two time instants. <p>From package UML::Values.</p>

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.DurationConstraint
files.Summary: A DurationConstraint is a Constraint that refers to a DurationInterval. <p>From package UML::Values.</p>

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.DurationInterval
files.Summary: A DurationInterval defines the range between two Durations. <p>From package UML::Values.</p>

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.DurationObservation.DurationObservationReferencedElementsCollection
files.Summary: The collection class to to represent the children of the DurationObservation class

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.DurationObservation
files.Summary: A DurationObservation is a reference to a duration during an execution. It points out the NamedElement(s) in the model to observe and whether the observations are when this NamedElement is entered or when it is exited. <p>From package UML::Values.</p>

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.Element.ElementChildrenCollection
files.Summary: The collection class to to represent the children of the Element class

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.Element.ElementReferencedElementsCollection
files.Summary: The collection class to to represent the children of the Element class

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.Element
files.Summary: An Element is a constituent of a model. As such, it has the capability of owning other Elements. <p>From package UML::CommonStructure.</p>

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.ElementImport.ElementImportReferencedElementsCollection
files.Summary: The collection class to to represent the children of the ElementImport class

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.ElementImport
files.Summary: An ElementImport identifies a NamedElement in a Namespace other than the one that owns that NamedElement and allows the NamedElement to be referenced using an unqualified name in the Namespace owning the ElementImport. <p>From package UML::CommonStructure.</p>

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.EncapsulatedClassifier.EncapsulatedClassifierChildrenCollection
files.Summary: The collection class to to represent the children of the EncapsulatedClassifier class

files.Summary: The collection class to to represent the children of the EncapsulatedClassifier class

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.EncapsulatedClassifier
files.Summary: An EncapsulatedClassifier may own Ports to specify typed interaction points. <p>From package UML::StructuredClassifiers.</p>

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.EncapsulatedClassifierOwnedAttributeCollection
files.Summary: The collection class to implement the refined ownedAttribute reference for the EncapsulatedClassifier class

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.Enumeration.EnumerationChildrenCollection
files.Summary: The collection class to to represent the children of the Enumeration class

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.Enumeration.EnumerationReferencedElementsCollection
files.Summary: The collection class to to represent the children of the Enumeration class

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.Enumeration
files.Summary: An Enumeration is a DataType whose values are enumerated in the model as EnumerationLiterals. <p>From package UML::SimpleClassifiers.</p>

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.EnumerationLiteral.EnumerationLiteralReferencedElementsCollection
files.Summary: The collection class to to represent the children of the EnumerationLiteral class

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.EnumerationLiteral
files.Summary: An EnumerationLiteral is a user-defined data value for an Enumeration. <p>From package UML::SimpleClassifiers.</p>

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.EnumerationOwnedLiteralCollection
files.Summary: Denotes a class to implement the ownedLiteral reference

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.Event
files.Summary: An Event is the specification of some occurrence that may potentially trigger effects by an object. <p>From package UML::CommonBehavior.</p>

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.ExceptionHandler.ExceptionHandlerReferencedElementsCollection
files.Summary: The collection class to to represent the children of the ExceptionHandler class

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.ExceptionHandler
files.Summary: An ExceptionHandler is an Element that specifies a handlerBody ExecutableNode to execute in case the specified exception occurs during the execution of the protected ExecutableNode. <p>From package UML::Activities.</p>

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.ExecutableNode.ExecutableNodeChildrenCollection
files.Summary: The collection class to to represent the children of the ExecutableNode class

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.ExecutableNode.ExecutableNodeReferencedElementsCollection
files.Summary: The collection class to to represent the children of the ExecutableNode class

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.ExecutableNode
files.Summary: An ExecutableNode is an abstract class for ActivityNodes whose execution may be controlled using ControlFlows and to which ExceptionHandlers may be attached. <p>From package UML::Activities.</p>

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.ExecutableNodeHandlerCollection
files.Summary: Denotes a class to implement the handler reference

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.ExecutionEnvironment
files.Summary: An execution environment is a node that offers an execution environment for specific types of components that are deployed on it in the form of executable artifacts. <p>From package UML::Deployments.</p>

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.ExecutionOccurrenceSpecification.ExecutionOccurrenceSpecificationReferencedElementsCollection
files.Summary: The collection class to to represent the children of the ExecutionOccurrenceSpecification class

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.ExecutionOccurrenceSpecification
files.Summary: An ExecutionOccurrenceSpecification represents moments in time at which Actions or Behaviors start or finish. <p>From package UML::Interactions.</p>

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.ExecutionSpecification.ExecutionSpecificationReferencedElementsCollection
files.Summary: The collection class to to represent the children of the ExecutionSpecification class

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.ExecutionSpecification
files.Summary: An ExecutionSpecification is a specification of the execution of a unit of Behavior or Action within the Lifeline. The duration of an ExecutionSpecification is represented by two OccurrenceSpecifications, the start OccurrenceSpecification and the finish OccurrenceSpecification. <p>From package UML::Interactions.</p>

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.ExpansionKind
files.Summary: ExpansionKind is an enumeration type used to specify how an ExpansionRegion executes its contents. <p>From package UML::Actions.</p>

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.ExpansionKindConverter
files.Summary: Implements a type converter for the enumeration ExpansionKind

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.ExpansionNode.ExpansionNodeReferencedElementsCollection
files.Summary: The collection class to to represent the children of the ExpansionNode class

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.ExpansionNode
files.Summary: An ExpansionNode is an ObjectNode used to indicate a collection input or output for an ExpansionRegion. A collection input of an ExpansionRegion contains a collection that is broken into its individual elements inside the region, whose content is executed once per element. A collection output of an ExpansionRegion combines individual elements produced by the execution of the region into a collection for use outside the region. <p>From package UML::Actions.</p>

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.ExpansionRegion.ExpansionRegionReferencedElementsCollection
files.Summary: The collection class to to represent the children of the ExpansionRegion class

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.ExpansionRegion
files.Summary: An ExpansionRegion is a StructuredActivityNode that executes its content multiple times corresponding to elements of input collection(s). <p>From package UML::Actions.</p>

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.ExpansionRegionInputElementCollection
files.Summary: Denotes a class to implement the inputElement reference

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.ExpansionRegionOutputElementCollection
files.Summary: Denotes a class to implement the outputElement reference

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.Expression.ExpressionChildrenCollection
files.Summary: The collection class to to represent the children of the Expression class

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.Expression.ExpressionReferencedElementsCollection
files.Summary: The collection class to to represent the children of the Expression class

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.Expression
files.Summary: An Expression represents a node in an expression tree, which may be non-terminal or terminal. It defines a symbol, and has a possibly empty sequence of operands that are ValueSpecifications. It denotes a (possibly empty) set of values when evaluated in a context. <p>From package UML::Values.</p>

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.Extend.ExtendChildrenCollection
files.Summary: The collection class to to represent the children of the Extend class

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.Extend.ExtendReferencedElementsCollection
files.Summary: The collection class to to represent the children of the Extend class

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.Extend
files.Summary: A relationship from an extending UseCase to an extended UseCase that specifies how and when the behavior defined in the extending UseCase can be inserted into the behavior defined in the extended UseCase. <p>From package UML::UseCases.</p>

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.Extension
files.Summary: An extension is used to indicate that the properties of a metaclass are extended through a stereotype, and gives the ability to flexibly add (and later remove) stereotypes to classes. <p>From package UML::Packages.</p>

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.ExtensionEnd
files.Summary: An extension end is used to tie an extension to a stereotype when extending a metaclass. The default multiplicity of an extension end is 0..1. <p>From package UML::Packages.</p>

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.ExtensionPoint.ExtensionPointReferencedElementsCollection
files.Summary: The collection class to to represent the children of the ExtensionPoint class

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.ExtensionPoint
files.Summary: An ExtensionPoint identifies a point in the behavior of a UseCase where that behavior can be extended by the behavior of some other (extending) UseCase, as specified by an Extend relationship. <p>From package UML::UseCases.</p>

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.Feature
files.Summary: A Feature declares a behavioral or structural characteristic of Classifiers. <p>From package UML::Classification.</p>

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.FinalNode
files.Summary: A FinalNode is an abstract ControlNode at which a flow in an Activity stops. <p>From package UML::Activities.</p>

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.FinalState
files.Summary: A special kind of State, which, when entered, signifies that the enclosing Region has completed. If the enclosing Region is directly contained in a StateMachine and all other Regions in that StateMachine also are completed, then it means that the entire StateMachine behavior is completed. <p>From package UML::StateMachines.</p>

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.FlowFinalNode
files.Summary: A FlowFinalNode is a FinalNode that terminates a flow by consuming the tokens offered to it. <p>From package UML::Activities.</p>

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.ForkNode
files.Summary: A ForkNode is a ControlNode that splits a flow into multiple concurrent flows. <p>From package UML::Activities.</p>

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.FunctionBehavior
files.Summary: A FunctionBehavior is an OpaqueBehavior that does not access or modify any objects or other external data. <p>From package UML::CommonBehavior.</p>

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.Gate
files.Summary: A Gate is a MessageEnd which serves as a connection point for relating a Message which has a MessageEnd (sendEvent / receiveEvent) outside an InteractionFragment with another Message which has a MessageEnd (receiveEvent / sendEvent) inside that InteractionFragment. <p>From package UML::Interactions.</p>

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.GeneralOrdering.GeneralOrderingReferencedElementsCollection
files.Summary: The collection class to to represent the children of the GeneralOrdering class

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.GeneralOrdering
files.Summary: A GeneralOrdering represents a binary relation between two OccurrenceSpecifications, to describe that one OccurrenceSpecification must occur before the other in a valid trace. This mechanism provides the ability to define partial orders of OccurrenceSpecifications that may otherwise not have a specified order. <p>From package UML::Interactions.</p>

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.Generalization.GeneralizationReferencedElementsCollection
files.Summary: The collection class to to represent the children of the Generalization class

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.Generalization
files.Summary: A Generalization is a taxonomic relationship between a more general Classifier and a more specific Classifier. Each instance of the specific Classifier is also an instance of the general Classifier. The specific Classifier inherits the features of the more general Classifier. A Generalization is owned by the specific Classifier. <p>From package UML::Classification.</p>

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.GeneralizationSet
files.Summary: A GeneralizationSet is a PackageableElement whose instances represent sets of Generalization relationships. <p>From package UML::Classification.</p>

files.Summary: Denotes a class to implement the generalization reference

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.InformationFlow
files.Summary: InformationFlows describe circulation of information through a system in a general manner. They do not specify the nature of the information, mechanisms by which it is conveyed, sequences of exchange or any control conditions. During more detailed modeling, representation and realization links may be added to specify which model elements implement an InformationFlow and to show how information is conveyed. InformationFlows require some kind of “information channel” for unidirectional transmission of information items from sources to targets.  They specify the information channel’s realizations, if any, and identify the information that flows along them.  Information moving along the information channel may be represented by abstract InformationItems and by concrete Classifiers. <p>From package UML::InformationFlows.</p>

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.InformationItem.InformationItemReferencedElementsCollection
files.Summary: The collection class to to represent the children of the InformationItem class

files.Title: NMF.Interop.Uml.InformationItem
files.Summary: InformationItems represent many kinds of information that can flow from sources to targets in very abstract ways.  They represent the kinds of information that may move within a system, but do not elaborate details of the transferred information.  Details of transferred information are the province of other Classifiers that may ultimately define InformationItems.  Consequently, InformationItems cannot be instantiated and do not themselves have features, generalizations, or associations. An important use of InformationItems is to represent information during early design stages, possibly before the detailed modeling decisions that will ultimately define them have been made. Another purpose of InformationItems is to abstract portions of complex models in less precise, but perhaps more general and communicable, ways. <p>From package UML::InformationFlows.</p>

files.Summary: An InstanceSpecification is a model element that represents an instance in a modeled system. It can also act as a DeployedArtifact, if it represents an instance of an Artifact. <p>From package UML::Classification.</p>
